## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Why this work is necessary and important
• We’re (hopefully) coming out of a once in a century event that disrupted
education on a scale not seen in our lifetimes.
• Evidence (and common sense) suggests that academic impacts of the
pandemic were NOT uniformly felt. Evidence suggests:
• Differential impact by content area
• Differential impact by demographic student group (e.g., ethnicity, SES)
• Differential impact by state, district, and school
• Differential impact by mode of education
• Differential impact by student academic subgroup (e.g., students receiving special education
services)
• Probably numerous other relevant groups.
• Ameliorating impact will necessary be targeted and require understanding
academic impact by these groups.
Understanding Indiana WIDA-ACCESS Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Interim Assessments FTW
• With the onset of the pandemic in spring 2020, state assessments (had they been
given) would have been of little use in determining academic impact.
• Interim assessments, often given in Fall, Winter, Spring we’re ideally timed to
investigate academic impact as of Fall 2020 and Winter 2021.
• Renaissance STAR assessments have a vertical, cross-grade, cross-year scale allowing
for pre-pandemic to pandemic comparison of student attainment.
• Renaissance STAR assessments have a baseline referenced growth measure to
compare (difference in difference) growth pre-pandemic to pandemic growth.
• Spring 2020 interim assessment data will be problematic to work with due to the
onset of the pandemic.
• State summative tests will be a critical piece of data in the coming weeks to help us
better understand the academic impact of the pandemic.
Understanding Indiana WIDA-ACCESS Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Transitioning from Impact to Recovery
• States are at different points of dealing with the pandemic and its
impact on education.
• Some students have returned to in-person learning early in the 2020-2021
academic year.
• Other students are still learning remotely.
• If the goal is to (at least) ameliorate the academic impact of the
pandemic on students, focus should be on finding ways to accelerate
student learning.
• A big concern going forward should be differential recovery where
(on average) the “haves” recover and the “have nots” don’t recover.
Understanding Indiana WIDA-ACCESS Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Tests are necessary but not sufficient
• Learning loss or unfinished learning? Assessments won’t tell us.
• Assessments (at their best) tell us where we are on our academic
journey. They don’t tell us how to get to our destination.
• With a clear understanding of the magnitude of the academic impact,
we can sensibly “right-size” efforts to recovery.
• Bigger impacts necessitate longer recovery times and (possibly) more
intensive interventions.
• Smaller impacts necessitate shorter recovery times and (possibly) less
intensive interventions.
• The data is there to guide us if we choose to use it sensibly!
Understanding Indiana WIDA-ACCESS Pandemic Related Academic Impact</div>
```
